result.summary: The section traces Pelasgus and his son Lycaon, whose fifty impious sons test Zeus by serving him human flesh and are struck down. It then tells how Callisto, a companion of Artemis, is seduced by Zeus, turned into a bear and killed, and how her son Arcas is saved.

scenes.title: Lycaon's impious sons
scenes.summary: Lycaon's fifty sons serve Zeus, disguised as a laborer, a slaughtered child. Zeus overturns the table and blasts them with thunderbolts, sparing only Nyctimus.
scenes.stakes: Lycaon and his sons risk destruction by Zeus's wrath for their impiety; only Nyctimus survives.

scenes.title: The flood of Deucalion
scenes.summary: Nyctimus inherits the kingdom, and the flood of Deucalion's age follows, which some blame on Lycaon's sons.

scenes.title: Callisto and Zeus
scenes.summary: Callisto, a sworn maiden hunter of Artemis, is seduced by Zeus and turned into a bear. She is shot by Artemis, her son Arcas goes to Maia, and she becomes the constellation of the Bear.
scenes.stakes: Callisto loses her maidenhood, her human form and finally her life.

notable_quotes.reason: Memorable image of Lycaon's sons serving a murdered child to Zeus.

analysis.text: Human impiety is tested and punished by Zeus, while divine desire leads to the suffering of mortals like Callisto.
Arcadian genealogies and cult tales, such as the Lycaon story, explain local names like Trapezus and link the region to its founders.

legacy.text: Callisto's story explains the constellation Ursa Major, and Lycaon's story lies behind the word lycanthropy in later tradition, as told by Ovid.

fun_facts.text: The text records several competing ancestries for Callisto, from Hesiod, Asius and Pherecydes, showing how varied Greek myth traditions were.

language_notes.text: Pelasgus is the legendary first man or ancestor of the Arcadians; the sources disagree about his parentage, as Acusilaus and Hesiod are cited against each other.
"Son of the soil" means born from the earth itself, an autochthonous (native-born) ancestor with no human parents.
"Mixed his bowels with the sacrifices" means the boy's entrails were put among the animal meats served to the guest, so he would unknowingly eat human flesh.
Trapezus means "table" in Greek, so the place name preserves the story of the overturned table.
The flood of Deucalion is the Greek flood myth in which Zeus destroyed the bronze race; Deucalion and Pyrrha survived.
"Maid" means virgin; followers of Artemis were bound to chastity.
The Bear is the constellation Ursa Major; Callisto's son Arcas gave his name to Arcadia.

context_notes.text: Lycaon was a legendary king of Arcadia, a mountainous region of the central Peloponnese. The long list of sons includes names of Arcadian towns and places.
Hera, Zeus's wife, was habitually jealous of his lovers and often punished them.
Maia, a nymph and daughter of Atlas, was the mother of Hermes by Zeus.

literary_notes.text: The long list of names is a traditional epic and genealogical device, conveying the scale of Lycaon's line and the extent of the coming destruction.
Earth acts as a person, seizing Zeus's hand to calm him, which explains why one son survives.
Zeus takes the form of Artemis, the goddess of chastity, to violate Callisto's vow, which makes the deception crueler.
